sections.h2: Does Indiana have its own capital gains tax on a house sale?
sections.html:
The Department of Revenue's rate page lists one individual rate and no separate capital gains rate for a house. The statute starts with federal adjusted gross income as defined in Section 62 of the Internal Revenue Code and then applies Indiana's own additions and subtractions, so a taxable gain that lands on your federal return flows into the state calculation.

The Department of Revenue lists the individual adjusted gross income tax rate at 2.95 percent for 2026 and 2.90 percent for 2027. That one rate applies to the whole income figure, gain included.

Counties add their own income tax on top. The Department's Departmental Notice #1, effective for periods beginning on or after October 1, 2026, lists Howard County at 0.0235, or 2.35 percent. For withholding, the notice ties a taxpayer to a county by residence on January 1, and the Department says county rates can be adjusted in January and October.

sections.h2: What does the federal home sale exclusion cover?
sections.html:
For most sellers, the federal exclusion decides whether any gain reaches the state calculation at all. The IRS says you can exclude up to $250,000 of gain, or $500,000 if you file jointly with a spouse, when you sell your main home.

The tests in IRS Topic 701 are specific:

  • You or your spouse owned the home for at least 24 months of the last 5 years.
  • The home was your residence for at least 24 months of the last 5 years, and both spouses must meet this test on a joint return.
  • You must meet both tests during the 5 years ending on the sale date, though the two 24-month periods can fall in different stretches.
  • You cannot use the exclusion if you excluded gain from another home sale within the previous two years.

If you receive a Form 1099-S, you report the sale even when the gain is fully excludable. When the exclusion does not cover everything, Schedule D and Form 8949 come into play. A person on qualified official extended duty can elect to suspend the five-year period for up to ten years.

sections.h2: How are gains above the exclusion taxed federally?
sections.html:
A gain on property held more than one year is long term, and the IRS taxes it at 0, 15 or 20 percent depending on taxable income. Gain on property held one year or less is short term and taxed as ordinary income.

The 2025 thresholds shown on the IRS capital gains page are below, and they change each year, so confirm the current ones before filing.

The same page says 20 percent applies above the 15 percent range, that unrecaptured section 1250 gain has a 25 percent maximum rate, and that people with significant investment income may owe the net investment income tax. It also states that a loss on the sale of a personal home is not deductible.

sections.h2: Which Indiana adjustments matter to someone selling a house?
sections.html:
The most useful one is a subtraction for property taxes paid on a principal residence, up to $2,500 ($1,250 for separate filers). It appears in the statute's list of subtractions from federal income, alongside Social Security benefits and certain military income.

The statute also lists additions, such as state income taxes deducted on the federal return and certain bonus depreciation and Section 179 amounts. Owners who depreciated a rental house should go through that list with a preparer.

Because Justia's copy of the code may lag behind the legislature, check the current Indiana tax booklet before relying on a dollar limit. The Department says individual filers find current county rates in the IT-40 booklet.

sections.h2: What if the house was inherited?
sections.html:
Gain on an inherited house is measured from a stepped-up starting value, which usually means much less taxable gain than the original purchase price would suggest. IRS Publication 551 says the basis of inherited property is its fair market value at the date of death, or the value on the alternate valuation date if the estate's personal representative elects that.

One exception applies: if you or your spouse gave appreciated property to the decedent within a year before death, your basis is the decedent's adjusted basis immediately before death. Keep the appraisal or the estate's valuation, since it becomes your cost figure when you report the sale.

Our separate Indiana estate and inheritance tax page covers the repealed state inheritance tax and how probate affects who can sign the deed.

sections.h2: What about a rental house or an investment property in Indiana?
sections.html:
The home sale exclusion applies to a main home, so a rental usually produces a taxable gain. The IRS says gain from real property that is unrecaptured section 1250 gain is taxed at a maximum of 25 percent.

Indiana then applies its rate to the federal income figure after the state's own modifications. Your total bill also depends on the federal bracket, the county rate and whether you qualify for the exclusion.

If a tenant occupies the house, the landlord's selling options and notice duties are separate questions, covered on our Indiana eviction process page.

sections.h2: How can you estimate the tax before you sell?
sections.html:
Start with arithmetic you can check yourself. Suppose a single filer has a $60,000 taxable gain above the exclusion, purely as an illustration. At the 2026 state rate of 2.95 percent, that gain adds $1,770 of Indiana tax, and the county rate in the Department's notice applies on top for a resident of the county it lists.

Gather these items before you ask a preparer to run numbers:

  • The purchase closing statement and receipts for capital improvements
  • The dates you moved in and moved out, to test the 24-month rules
  • Any prior home sale where you used the exclusion
  • The date of death and valuation, if you inherited
  • Records of depreciation, if the house was ever a rental
  • Your county of residence on January 1

faqs.q: What is the Indiana tax rate on gain from selling a house?
faqs.a: Indiana taxes the gain through its individual adjusted gross income tax, which the Department of Revenue sets at 2.95 percent for 2026 and 2.90 percent for 2027. Your county adds its own income tax rate on top.

faqs.q: Does Indiana tax the portion of gain that the federal exclusion covers?
faqs.a: Indiana begins with federal adjusted gross income, so gain you exclude federally does not appear in that starting figure. The statute's later modifications can still change the result, so a preparer should check your return.

faqs.q: How much gain can I exclude when I sell my main home?
faqs.a: Up to $250,000, or $500,000 on a joint return, if you meet the ownership and residence tests in 24 of the 60 months before the sale and have not used the exclusion within two years.

faqs.q: Is a house I inherited taxed on the original purchase price?
faqs.a: No. Under IRS Publication 551 the basis is generally the fair market value at the date of death, so gain is measured from that value. Gifts to the decedent within one year of death are an exception.

faqs.q: Does Howard County, Indiana charge a different income tax rate?
faqs.a: Departmental Notice #1 lists Howard County at 0.0235, or 2.35 percent, for periods beginning on or after October 1, 2026. County rates can change in January and October.

faqs.q: Do I report the sale if the gain is excludable?
faqs.a: Yes, if you receive a Form 1099-S. The IRS says to report the sale even when the gain is excludable. Schedule D and Form 8949 are used when you cannot exclude all of the gain.
